title: Two-column role frictions — candidate notes (Kai Martin)
content:
Quick scratch: two-column mental model for Kai Martin (phone + pairing). Purpose: capture raw strengths vs frictions so I can verbatim paste into handoff and track unresolved asks.

LEFT (Signals / Strengths)
- Clear mental model for KV cache and why persistent caches are hard at scale — used concrete latency numbers in pairing.
- Good familiarity with beam/greedy tradeoffs for reranking; suggested hybrid that reduced top-1 regressions in his example.
- Pragmatic infra instincts: prioritizes observable invariants over gold-plated design early in rollout.
- Cultural fit: measured, asks clarifying questions, pushes for small experiments first.
- Communication: good at drawing quick ascii diagrams; paired well when debugging a sticky OOM.

RIGHT (Frictions / Risks)
- Less depth in C++ kernel optimization; mostly Python + CUDA wrappers. Risk if we need low-level kernel work.
- Limited exposure to quantization internals (LUT/FP16 edge cases). Relied on vendor libs in past role.
- On canary + rollback patterns: described ad-hoc scripts rather than rollout orchestration; will need shepherding to adopt our rollout rig.
- Slight overconfidence on performance extrapolation from toy workloads -> flagged with follow-up tests.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (to follow up)
- Has he shipped a production fallback (model variant) at p99 tail latencies for multi-tenant infra? example timeline?
- Can he show a short snippet of a kernel or a profiling output where he found a surprising hotspot? (ask for a short gisted example)

QUICK SCORE (0-5) on key levers
- Core latency intuition: 4
- Kernel-level optimization: 2.5
- Pragmatic infra/runbook thinking: 4
- Team fit / communication: 4

HOLDING RECOMMENDATION (notes-to-self)
- Strong candidate for an SRE-adjacent runtime engineer vs a pure kernel engineer. If we need deep kernel hires, flag as partial-match.
- Recommend a short follow-up: 30m deep-dive on a profiling snippet + 20m systems interview to probe rollback/observability knowledge.

SUGGESTED PAIRING EXERCISE (for next round)
- Give a small microservice that degrades at high sequence lengths; ask candidate to: a) instrument to find culprit, b) propose a mitigation plan that preserves 95th pct latency SLO, c) explain tradeoffs.

TINY RAMP PLAN (if hired)
- Week 0-4: onboarding + reproduce a small perf report; pair on one canary.
- Month 1-3: own a single-model rollout (latency/cost dashboard) and run a quantization validation.

NOTES TO SELF: paste into handoff doc with headline: "Strong infra pragmatist, limited kernel depth — good hire for routing/batching/caching ownership; needs mentorship on low-level kernels."

End of note. Kept short on purpose so handoff is copyable.
